served.stem: Two carbonyls are available for reduction by NaBH4 in methanol: acetophenone (an aryl methyl ketone, drawn) and benzaldehyde. Considering electronic and steric effects on hydride addition, which statement about relative rate is correct?
choices: Acetophenone is reduced faster because ketones are inherently more electrophilic than aldehydes at the carbonyl carbon in every solvent
Benzaldehyde is reduced faster than acetophenone because the aldehyde carbonyl is less hindered and more electrophilic
Both are reduced at identical rates because NaBH4 reacts only with esters
Neither reacts because NaBH4 cannot reduce conjugated aryl carbonyls
Acetophenone is reduced faster because the extra methyl group donates electron density that makes the carbonyl a better hydride acceptor
served.bankWhy: Aldehydes are reduced faster than ketones by hydride: the aldehyde carbonyl carbon is less sterically hindered and more electrophilic (only one alkyl/aryl group donating electron density), so benzaldehyde reacts faster than the more hindered, more electron-rich acetophenone.

answer.text: Benzaldehyde is reduced faster than acetophenone because the aldehyde carbonyl is less hindered and more electrophilic
answer.line: The aldehyde carbon carries an H where the ketone carries a methyl: more room and more plus charge, so hydride arrives faster.

steps: Compare what sits on each carbonyl carbon. Benzaldehyde has a phenyl and an H; acetophenone has a phenyl and a methyl.
The methyl pushes electron density in, so that carbon is less positive. It also crowds the path hydride takes in.
NaBH4 reduces both. The question is speed, and the aldehyde goes first.

choices.text: Acetophenone is reduced faster because ketones are inherently more electrophilic than aldehydes at the carbonyl carbon in every solvent
choices.note: Ketones are the less electrophilic of the two. Two carbon groups donate more than one, so the order runs the other way.

choices.text: Benzaldehyde is reduced faster than acetophenone because the aldehyde carbonyl is less hindered and more electrophilic
choices.note: Less hindered and more electrophilic: both reasons point the same way, toward the aldehyde.

choices.text: Both are reduced at identical rates because NaBH4 reacts only with esters
choices.note: NaBH4 is the mild hydride: it reduces aldehydes and ketones and walks past most esters. LiAlH4 is the one that takes esters.

choices.text: Neither reacts because NaBH4 cannot reduce conjugated aryl carbonyls
choices.note: NaBH4 does leave the benzene ring and isolated C=C bonds alone. The C=O next to the ring is still a target, and it gets reduced.

choices.text: Acetophenone is reduced faster because the extra methyl group donates electron density that makes the carbonyl a better hydride acceptor
choices.note: The methyl does donate electron density. But donation makes the carbonyl carbon less positive, a worse hydride acceptor, not a better one.

student.lockIt: Aldehydes beat ketones to a nucleophile: one carbon group means more room and more plus charge.
